implementation_notes: Spring Integration implements the pattern rather than just carrying it: declaring @EnableMessageHistory (or the <message-history/> element) makes every named component write the 'history' header, a List<Properties> of {name, type, timestamp} entries, and tracked-components restricts tracking to matching names. Since 6.3 the header is append-only - the first track creates a new message with a MessageHistory container and later writes append in place - and multi-output components (PublishSubscribeChannel, routers, WireTap, splitter) clone the header so parallel branches do not share one list. Read it with message.getHeaders().get(MessageHistory.HEADER_NAME, MessageHistory.class); the classic envelope-plus-hooks structure is replaced by configuration.
pitfalls: Exactly one @EnableMessageHistory (or <message-history/>) may be declared, and the configurer must not be defined as a generic bean - a second source of tracking configuration breaks tracking.
Pre-6.3 semantics copied the entire message on every track, so enable tracking selectively (tracked-components) or per environment; the append-only behaviour is the performance-relevant fix.
Multi-producing flows outside the framework must clone the history (the framework's cloneMessageHistoryIfAny helper) or sibling branches append into a shared list.
